newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING-SILVER CHARM SEEKS GOLD AT BELMONT.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SILVER CHARM SEEKS GOLD AT BELMONT.

text.p: Kentucky Derby and Preakness winner Silver Charm arrived at Belmont Park on Wednesday to make final preparations in his bid to become only the 12th horse in racing history to win the Triple Crown.
"He's so relaxed and confident," trainer Bob Baffert said after the horse was settled in his stall. "He's got that look Michael Jordan had when he hit that game-winner the other night."

A small fortune will be on the line at Saturday's Belmont Stakes and not just the $5 million guarantee to Silver Charm's owners if the horse adds the third jewel of the series, an accomplishment no horse has achieved since Affirmed in 1978.
The value in breeding rights to Silver Charm is incalculable, especially since the horse is from connections considered less than regal.

Silver Charm was bred in Florida by Mary Lou Wooton. Though he is considered unfashionably bred, by Silver Buck out of Bonnie's Poker, he was picked to win the Derby and Preakness on the basis of his breeding by the Daily Racing Form's bloodline specialist, Ed Fountaine.

"He's unfashionable in the sense that the two most fashionable sires at the sales are Northern Dancer and Mr. Prospector," Fountaine said, "and he doesn't have an ounce of Northern Dancer in him. No Mr. Prospector either."

What Silver Charm does have is stamina and fitness, qualities that Fountaine thinks will guarantee a victory in the 1 1/2 mile Belmont -- the longest of the Triple Crown races -- and a fortune in the breeding shed.
"He's the one horse in the race that you can't find a knock on going 1 1/2 miles," said Fountaine. "If he gets beat I don't know what it will be."
Silver Charm's lack of fashionable pedigree is exactly what makes a Triple Crown sweep so potentially valuable at stud.
"Seattle Slew was unfashionably bred too, but now you look at him and he is fashionable," Fountaine said. "Silver Crown has got to be in demand as a sire because he'll be a tremendous outcross.
"Almost every horse you see now is inbred. As a Triple crown winner he could easily command $50,000 a foal first time out."

Silver Charm is scheduled to face six rivals in Saturday's race, but he had to overcome a scare in his last workout for the Belmont, when he narrowly avoided a disastrous collision with a loose horse on the Churchill Downs track Tuesday morning.
Nevertheless, the colt looked none the worse for wear when he arrived at his stall on the Belmont backstretch after being vanned to the track from Kennedy airport with a police escort.
The main challenge to Silver Charm was expected to come from Free House, who finished second in the Preakness and third in the Derby.
"Free House is the horse to beat," Baffert said. "He's the one who probably worries me the most."

Free House and Silver Charm have met five times, with Silver Charm posting wins in the San Vicente Stakes, Kentucky Derby and Preakness, and Free House emerging victorious in the San Felipe Stakes and Santa Anita Derby.
